newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro shares cede gains after Wall St slips.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro shares cede gains after Wall St slips.

text.p: European shares went into retreat, shedding most of the gains they made during the morning when Wall Street opened weaker and contined to fall.
The dollar was also facing an uphill battle to recoup some of the heavy losses it suffered against the yen on Thursday.
The Dow Jones industrial index of top U.S. shares was down around 50 points after an hour of trading following stronger-than-expected figures on U.S. housing starts.

Total starts were up 2.6 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.47 million in April after a revised 7.7 percent drop to 1.43 million in March, the U.S. government said. Analysts had forecast a rate of 1.43 million.
London's FTSE 100 shed most of the day's strong rise and fell back below psychologically key 4,700 points level.
The index was up just 9.5 points at 4,690.7 at 1430 GMT.

It hit a fresh intra-day high of 4,723.7 immediately before the expiry of FTSE options during the morning as stock shortages continued and amid position-closing ahead of the weekend and Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy setting Federal Open Market Committee.
"We're just going to see the market kicking its heels until Tuesday," said one dealer.
The majority of economists believe the U.S. central bank will raise rates to forestall the threat of inflation.
French stocks also retreated after flirting with the 2,800-point mark at midday. They were down 0.45 of a percent at 2,775.56 at 1430 gmt.

The CAC-40 index briefly hit an all time high of 2,800.84 during the morning, bolstered by gains in bond prices, Wall Street's gains overnight and a fresh Ipsos poll showing the conservatives leading in the upcoming parliamentary election.

The Ipsos poll for the magazine Le Point projected the ruling RPR-UDF coalition would win 323 seats in the 577-member National Assembly, up from 290 in a similar poll last week. It indicated the Socialists would trail with 266 seats.
In Frankfurt, the DAX index ended with a gain of 42.44 points, or 1.2 percent, at 3,604.55 underpinned by Wall Street's overnight close and the dollar's foray above 1.70 marks.
But the DAX had closed before Wall Street opened and the DAX Ibis index of electronic trading was up just 9.75 at 3,574.60 at 1430 gmt.

In currencies, the dollar traded slightly firmer against the mark and yen early in Europe as the markets stabilised following a volatile week of sharp yen gains and shifting interest rate expectations in Japan and the United States.
The rally soon faltered however and the U.S. currency stood at around 115.40 yen, well off its overnight high of 117.00 yen, and at 1.6975 marks at 1430 gmt.
Traders in Tokyo said the overnight session was dominated by a reaction to this week's steep decline in dollar/yen which was seen to be overdone. The recovery was limited and capped at 117 yen.
"Things are calmer and people seem to be digesting what was a very eventful week. We're starting to focus now on the FOMC next week," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago.
The dollar/yen has collapsed from 4-1/2-year highs this month and lost almost 10 percent of its value in just two weeks.

The reversal was triggered by a barrage of verbal intervention from Japanese officials aimed at preventing the yen weakening further and hastening the need for higher Japanese interest rates. Growing speculation about a rise Japanese rates, nevertheless, has reinforced the yen recovery, said analysts.
STOCK PRICES AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 9.5 points at 4,690.7.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 0.45 points at 2,775.56.
Frankfurt's DAX index ended up 42.44 points at 3,604.55.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6975 marks and 115.40 yen compared with 1.6986 marks and 116.26 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold fixed at $344.50 in the afternoon compared with $347.00 in the morning session and London's close of $346.95 on Thursday. It slipped under $345 support after the New York opening, following silver lower. Silver suffered sharp losses on U.S. selling and was off 16 cents at $4.70.
